title: access-schema-evolution-test-harness-and-siem-adapter
body:
Purpose:
This doc defines a lightweight test harness and SIEM adapter prototype to validate the RBAC v2 access schema evolution plan and evidence automation export. The focus is on repeatable deterministic test cases, event sampling strategy, and mappings to both Splunk and Chronicle. This is intended to be a living working doc for eng + sec before we formalize the rollout playbook.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Synthetic access trace generator for role/permission mutation tests
- Canonical audit event model for RBAC v2 (fields, semantics, and signing expectations)
- SIEM adapter mapping and sample search queries (Splunk/Chronicle)
- Evidence envelope lifecycle (creation -> TTL -> archival) and automation hooks
- Canary and staged rollout test plan + rollback criteria

Out of scope:
- Full data retention legal/PII policy (refer to compliance-retention-policy)
- KMS/HSM implementation details (KMS team owns key ops)

Design goals:
- Determinism: tests must be replayable and produce identical evidence envelopes for the same seed input.
- Minimal perturbation: production audit pipeline should accept RBAC v2 events without changes when using compatibility mode.
- Observability: each step must attach correlating ids so we can trace request -> adjudication -> enforcement -> evidence export.
- SIEM-friendly: event payloads structured so Splunk/Chronicle parsers can extract principal, resource, action, result, and confidence effortlessly.

High-level flow (test harness):
1) Seed generator produces a suite of synthetic requests: CRUD on resources, delegated claims issuance, JIT token issuance, timebound grants, and session escalation. Each request has: principal_id, request_id (uuid v7), trace_id, timestamp, and expected_decision.
2) RBAC engine applies current policy graph + attribute resolution service. Decision recorded as decision_event.
3) Evidence envelope created (signed metadata + compact claim set) and written to evidence-store (S3-like). Evidence index event emitted to audit-stream.
4) Audit-stream goes through the SIEM adapter which enriches and maps fields to SIEM schema. Test harness captures both pre-adapter and post-adapter payloads for diffing.

Canonical audit event model (proposal):
- event_id: string (uuid v7)
- event_time: ISO-8601 UTC
- trace_id: string (hex64)
- request_id: string
- principal: { id: string, principal_type: string }  <-- note: for clarity in examples only; final payload must be flat for SIEM
- resource: string (resource canonical path)
- action: string (e.g., read, write, grant, revoke)
- decision: allow|deny|deferred|fallback
- decision_reason: short code (e.g., policy-miss, attribute-mismatch, delegated-claim, cache-hit)
- policy_snapshot: string (policy schema version or commit sha)
- evidence_ref: string (object key or signed URL)
- evidence_hash: sha256 hex
- evidence_ttl_seconds: int
- actor_ip: ipv4/ipv6
- auxiliary_tags: comma separated list
- signature: compact JWS (compact serialization)

Note on flattening: while the canonical model above uses nested fields for readability, the exported audit log MUST be flattened for SIEM ingestion using dot-notation keys (e.g., principal.id -> principal_id). The SIEM adapter will also emit a key 'canonical_model_version' so downstream parsers can evolve.

Sample minimal exported event (newline-separated JSON for clarity):
{
  "event_id": "e7f3c2d4-9a12-4b5f-a123-9cd8b4f7b111",
  "event_time": "2025-01-18T21:17:08Z",
  "trace_id": "1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d",
  "request_id": "r-20250118-0001",
  "principal_id": "user:marco.li@redwood.ai",
  "principal_type": "human",
  "resource": "projects/p-42/datasets/d-9",
  "action": "read",
  "decision": "allow",
  "decision_reason": "policy-allow",
  "policy_snapshot": "policy-2025-01-10-shaabcdef",
  "evidence_ref": "s3://evidence-prod/2025/01/18/e7f3c2d4.json",
  "evidence_hash": "b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184",
  "evidence_ttl_seconds": "7776000",
  "actor_ip": "34.120.45.2",
  "auxiliary_tags": "canary,rbac-evo",
  "signature": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "canonical_model_version": "v1.1-test-harness"
}

Evidence envelope format (compact guide):
- envelope_id (uuid)
- created_at
- signed_metadata: { principal_id, resource, action, decision, policy_snapshot } signed with platform-signing-key
- payload_ref: pointer to the full audit blob stored in evidence-store (compressed)
- hash_alg: sha256
- signature: base64url

Key automation expectations:
- Evidence indexer must be idempotent (replay same event_id => no duplicate index entries).
- Evidence TTL default = 90 days; can be overridden per-customer for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Automation job to snapshot and archive evidence older than TTL to cold store (retention policy will be a follow-up doc).
- Signed envelopes should include signer_kid and signer_role (platform, delegated-service, customer-proxy).

SIEM adapter mapping notes:
- Splunk: use _time=event_time, sourcetype=rbac_v2_audit, host=evidence-adapter-prod. Index a flattened JSON event + raw_evidence_ref. Also emit metric events (decision_latency_ms).
- Chronicle: map to findings with custom fields: principal_id, resource_path, action, decision, evidence_hash. Use chunked uploads for bulk replay.
- Sampling: canary mode -> 100% with full envelopes; ramp stage -> 10% full + 90% headers-only (headers-only = just indexes and evidence_ref). Production steady-state -> 1% full by default, rest headers-only. Sampling rates configurable per-tenant and per-route.

Test matrix (initial):
- Basic allow/deny: 100 synthetic requests, verify deterministic signatures and evidence_hash match expected.
- Delegation scenarios: generate delegated-claim issuance + consumption, verify chain-of-custody in envelope.
- Temporal grants: create timebound grants, replay after expiration and ensure decision flips to deny and evidence archived appropriately.
- Concurrency stress: 10k replay requests to audit-stream with purposefully shuffled timestamps to validate idempotency and ordering heuristics.
- SIEM ingestion tests: feed adapter with mixed sampling, validate Splunk sourcetypes and Chronicle fields.

Canary and rollout plan (high-level):
- Phase 0 (lab): harness + local adapter run by sec-eng, baseline tests green.
- Phase 1 (internal): light canary in staging stack -> 100% events to test indexer only. Duration: 1 week.
- Phase 2 (customer-internal): enable adapter for internal tenants (redwood-infra, dev-platform) with sampling 100% for 48h, then 10% for 5 days.
- Phase 3 (public ramp): enable for 10% of production tenants (headers-only 90% / full 10%) for 2 weeks, monitor false positives/false negatives in forensics queries.
- Phase 4 (full): flip default sampling to 1% full with ability to opt-in tenants for full retention.

Rollback criteria (stop-and-revert triggers):
- Evidence indexer duplicates >0.5% of events in production index in 1h window.
- SIEM ingestion errors causing >500 5xxs/min or backpressure spikes.
- Customers report incorrect enforcement observable in telemetry (decision disagreement rate >0.1%).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to include attribute-resolution snapshot in compact envelope without leaking PII? (Priya to propose redaction strategy)
- Confirm signer_kid rotation cadence with KMS team (ENG-4219).
- Decide canonical model versioning policy: semantic tags vs date+sha.
- Define standard Splunk saved-search templates for common investigations (compromise, privilege-escalation, mass-grant).

Implementation tasks & owners:
- Test harness generator (Marco Li) - GH-ISSUE-GH-7682 - target: PoC in 2 weeks.
- Evidence indexer idempotency patch (Daniel Kim) - PR: GH-PR-5901 - review by sec-eng.
- SIEM adapter prototype (Sofia Martinez) - map Splunk/Chronicle - deliver raw->flatten transform.
- Compliance signoff + retention knobs (Priya Rao) - coordinate with legal + KMS.

Quick actionable checklist (for next sync):
- [ ] Finalize flattened key names and publish mapping doc (Sofia)
- [ ] Add deterministic-seed mode to harness (Marco)
- [ ] Create Splunk test index and saved searches (DevOps)
- [ ] Run 1k synthetic replay against staging audit pipeline (all)
- [ ] Document evidence_archival playbook and retention levels (Priya)

Appendix A: example Splunk query snippets (for playbook):
- Find denies for a principal in last 24h:
  index=rbac_v2 sourcetype=rbac_v2_audit principal_id="user:marco.li@redwood.ai" decision=deny | stats count by resource action decision_reason

- High-volume allow events in last hour (suspicion of runaway automation):
  index=rbac_v2 sourcetype=rbac_v2_audit decision=allow | timechart span=1m count by principal_id limit=20

Appendix B: risk register (brief):
- Risk: evidence signing delays add >20ms to hot request path. Mitigation: async signing and publish signed envelope when available; export unsigned header immediately with placeholder.
- Risk: SIEM storage costs due to full-envelopes. Mitigation: sampling + customer opt-in for full retention.

Notes to self: keep this intentionally lightweight so eng teams can iterate. Prefer concrete tests over long prose. Expect multiple follow-ups: retention policy, KMS rotation, and dedicated tenant hooks for private deployments.

End of doc.
